title: Layout-flow benchmark protocol: draw-only vs gen-only vs gen+refine
description: Frozen protocol for the three-arm layout-generation benchmark (epic #2252, phase 1 = #3024). Methodology after Ding, Zou, Sun, Cong, 'Can Agents Design Better Chips with a Higher Level Abstraction?' (ICCAD'26; artifact github.com/ZijD/AHRR, MIT) -- methodology only, no code reuse. Phases 2-4 (#3025 task corpus, #3026 executor, #3027 reporting) consume this document; changing any decision here is a protocol_version bump and invalidates comparisons across versions.

tool_recording.description: Every tool call is made through the benchmark's own `bin/klt` shim (the one the interactive provider already puts on PATH), which appends one record per call to the run's `tool_calls` and refuses -- recording the call, exit code 126 -- any verb outside the current phase's allowed classes. The agent sandbox exposes no other geometry writer (no raw pya/gdstk/klayout, no hand-written stream bytes), so the recorded calls are the complete write path of the scored artifact.

arms.description: The agent places primitives and polygons directly with `klt draw`. No generator verb is available.
The agent parameterizes `klt gen` / `klt gen-compose`; the tools emit all geometry. No direct-geometry verb is available.

arms.analog: AHRR flow (ii)+(iii): HLS then RTL refinement
arms.description: Starts from a generator-built layout and may then edit freely with the union of both tool surfaces. There is no generate-from-scratch phase of its own: generation skill is measured by gen-only, refinement skill by the delta over that seed.

seeding_decision.question: Is gen+refine seeded from the same agent's gen-only best, or from a fixed reference composition? (#2252 open question 1)
seeding_decision.rationale: Matches AHRR's choice and measures the end-to-end flow an agent actually runs. The seed is content-addressed (sha256 of the stream) and recorded in the gen+refine run as `seed_from`, and it is part of that run's seed identity, so the dependency is reproducible from the ledgers alone. A fixed reference composition would isolate refinement skill but make the arm independent of the agent's generation skill; it may be added later as an ablation without changing this protocol's arms.
seeding_decision.reproducibility_check: A gen+refine run is only valid when its `seed_from` names a `valid` gen-only run of the same (task, agent, replicate) whose artifact hash equals `seed_from.gds_sha256`, and its score may not be worse than that seed's (the seed is round zero of the refine phase). All three are mechanically checked by `validate-layout`.
seeding_decision.measurement_outcome: no_blocker_found: the seed is a single immutable GDS identified by hash, so there is nothing non-reproducible to fall back from.

refinement_sufficiency.question: Does `klt draw` today expose enough edit primitives for a fair refinement arm? (#2252 open question 2)
evidence: `klt draw` read-modify-write mode (#3378): `params.base_gds` starts from an existing stream and `params.erase_um` windows remove its geometry before `shapes` are added (docs/cli/draw.md `base_gds`/`erase_um`), so a seeded shape can be trimmed or replaced in place.
The response reports `erased_shape_count` / `erased_label_count` when `base_gds` is given, so an erase is observable in the recorded call.

Additive refinement is also still expressible: `klt gen-compose` places the seed as a `blocks[].cell` library cell next to a `klt draw` patch cell and routes between them (docs/cli/gen-compose.md, #1189).
refinement_sufficiency.consequence: gen+refine is run with both the additive and the subtractive surface; no additive-only disclosure is required in reports.

task_eligibility.description: A task enters the comparison only if every rule holds; a task failing any rule is excluded from all three arms, never from just one, so arms stay comparable.

rules.description: Ships a frozen schematic netlist with a sha256 and no layout; the netlist is the LVS reference and is never taken from the agent's sandbox.
Ships a repo-frozen reference layout that is DRC-clean and LVS-clean against the frozen netlist under the frozen decks, so the task is satisfiable.
Ships a `klt gen`/`klt gen-compose` recipe that reaches a valid layout, so the gen-only arm is satisfiable without any direct-geometry verb.
Ships at least one known-bad layout per failing check (DRC and/or LVS) that the validity gate must reject, so the gate cannot be vacuously satisfied.
Targets an open PDK (sky130 first); no proprietary PDK data or NDA'd rules.

validity.description: Frozen validity gate. A run is scored only if every required check passes on the scored artifact.

provenance.rule: The sha256 of the scored GDS equals the gds_sha256 recorded in the DRC report, the LVS report, and the run's artifact; the LVS report's netlist_sha256 equals the task's frozen netlist sha256.

validity.note: The scorer re-runs drc/lvs itself on the harness's private copy of the artifact against repo-frozen decks and netlists; checks the agent ran in its sandbox are never trusted (same posture as round mode's read-only submissions copy).

fields.deferred: blocked on RC extraction (#217); null until then

score.aggregate: geomean of per-task area ratio over comparable pairs
score.comparable_pair: Both runs in the pair are valid for the same (task, agent, replicate); denominators are always reported.

failure_semantics.description: Only `valid` runs carry a score. Every other status is recorded, auditable, and unscored -- never a partial score.

seed_identity.description: Each run's identity is a hash of everything that defines it, so an unstable or reused seed is detectable from the record alone.

repeatability.deterministic_scope: Everything after the agent: the scorer re-run on a stored artifact must reproduce status, validity checks, and area_um2 exactly, and a report regenerated from ledgers alone must be byte-identical. Agent output itself is not expected to repeat; replicates measure its spread.

budget.description: Live-agent budget policy, built on the existing provider/ledger interfaces (#1739 interactive provider, #2253 round ledger, #2294 token usage; CI cost lessons from #1781). Deterministic validation needs no credentials.
budget.accounting: Per-run cost is the existing ledger `usage` object (tool_calls, turns, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache buckets) copied verbatim into the run record; no new meter is introduced.
